findings: HLM11 constructs one well-defined scalar action on the directed union via common-level relations; algebraic character projections commute with the group action and retain a nonzero vector.
HLM12 finite isotypic projections preserve earlier factors; semisimple character equality transfers the same Galois representation and all WOT bridges.
HLM13 matches every piPts_n_alt field at each nonzero module vector, including additive specialization on the entire union, exact scalar/group maps and every IsRecT.
HLM14 retains the exact abstract hypotheses and assembles the same maps without introducing a conditional replacement for the actual HLM24 producer.
HLM15-17 preserve actual residual/local data, every Teichmuller family, original integral type and exact function-level subgroup equality; maximal compact at conjugate places is accounted for.

HLM18-20 use faithful finite modules and a nonzero projective idempotent summand before specialization; no unjustified faithful or flat base change is assumed. The norm<1 coefficient condition is clopen in Qbar_ell and extends from the retained dense Frobenius set.
HLM21-22 keep full determinant laws via HLM6 and the unique-map universal property; the comparison map need not be surjective.
HLM23 uses one base before all auxiliary choices, with D=n[L+:Q], the original annihilator equal to J and exact weight-coordinate equations.
HLM24 constructs all auxiliary universal rings/pairs and actual IsJ maps from the inherited original foundations and already proved HLM9; no new all-level installation assumption remains.
HLM25 directly matches every LevMod, LevPtAlt and ClassicalAlt field, including quotient group action/projectivity and fixed iota separation.
HLM26 preserves all original quantifiers, including q=0, zero old module, prime3 and every positive rank. No mathematical correction requested.
record.scope: Full independent mathematical/source review HLM11-HLM26. HLM1-HLM10 and retained KX/local/automorphic foundations are inherited and separately reviewed, not reproved here.

findings: HLM1 writes an actual group-algebra projective splitting and the norm kernel, without division by the group order.
HLM2-3 use the original Neat stabilizer equality, all ambient equations and the ordinary projector to produce the trace criterion; the norm target and kernel match ordProj.
HLM4 gives the explicit Artin-Rees filtration argument and the original commuting residual projector.
HLM5 constructs the representation on one directed union of actual functions and identifies every fixed module; projectivity retains the exact source faithfulness condition.

HLM6 interpolation uses compactness only before iota, finite-degree truncated scalar algebras for all determinant-word computations, and polynomial coefficient separation rather than tensor-injectivity.
HLM7 constructs the full determinant and ordinary characters before calling a point theorem which assumes them; it includes abstract rank zero.
HLM8 uses actual algebra generation and injectivity to restrict Hecke operators, then exact IsUniv uniqueness to glue actions.

HLM9 constructs every pair field, including IsPsi.mu via the original Lambda.inert extension and the torsion-free unramified quotient; surjectivity follows from all Hecke generators and the compatible weight scalars.
HLM10 makes the universal action independent of the level and equivariant on the entire union. The two earlier requested clarifications in HLM6 and9 have been implemented.
record.scope: Independent mathematical and literal original-contract review of the enumerated claims only; other claims have separate peer reviews. Original named foundations remain in scope; no Lean replay.
